quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving.
Yes, if you are in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or have open alcohol in a vehicle on any public road. You cannot have an open alcohol container in areas where the driver or passengers sit.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: A curve in the road ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A curve in the road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that the road curves to the right.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it mean on a regulatory sign?

options.text: Some drivers must yield to others.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means an action is forbidden. These signs are white and rectangular with red and black markings.

questions.question: Is alcohol the leading cause of fatal car crashes?
questions.explanation: Alcohol is the top killer on American roads. It weakens vision and slows reaction time. Even small amounts of alcohol affect driving ability.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it may help prevent a crash.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a crash.
questions.explanation: Use your horn only to avoid crashes. Do not use it to tell a slow driver to speed up or get out of your way.

questions.question: What does this sign show?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that a T intersection is coming.

questions.question: What color lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
questions.explanation: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections, even without traffic lights or crosswalks.

questions.question: Is it illegal to drive at night using only parking lights?
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive at night using only parking lights. You must use your headlights when driving in the dark.

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are only in construction zones.
They are usually red and blue.

questions.explanation: Highway markings guide drivers on correct positioning, show safe passing zones, and warn about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong black coffee to stay awake.
They can drive so poorly that they may look drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can drive so poorly that they may look drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they appear drunk. Opening a window, turning on the radio, or drinking coffee is not enough to keep a drowsy driver alert to road dangers.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Your safety and others' safety depend on what you do before driving. Before moving your vehicle, adjust your seat, mirrors, and safety belt. Secure any items in or on your vehicle. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When there isn't room on the other side to completely cross the tracks.
When the crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
When you are transporting two or more young children in a passenger vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there isn't room on the other side to completely cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can be on any track at any time, traveling in either direction. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop. Do not stop on the tracks.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep downhill grade is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic signal is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What should drivers do when using a roundabout or traffic circle?

options.text: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with traffic moving counterclockwise around a center island. There is usually no traffic signal. Drivers entering must yield to traffic already in the roundabout. Follow the circle to the right until you reach your exit.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Rely only on the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
Rely only on the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot. You may need to look several times. Watch both the traffic ahead and the traffic in the lane next to you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Drivers must bear either right or left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must bear either right or left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road splits ahead and you must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign shows that a divided highway is starting ahead. The road splits into two separate one-way roads with a median between them. Stay to the right.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means an intersection is coming up. Watch carefully for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: What can help drivers save gas?

options.text: Leaving their car running in the driveway.

questions.explanation: Hard braking wastes fuel because you must accelerate again to match traffic speed. If you look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid braking, you use less gas.

questions.question: You do not need to follow a motorcycle as far back as you follow a car.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles stop faster than cars in dry conditions. You should stay 3 to 4 seconds behind a motorcycle to give the rider time to react in an emergency.

questions.question: When must you use your headlights?

options.text: Only when it is freezing cold.
During the day in good weather.

questions.explanation: You must use your headlights from sunset to sunrise. Use low beams instead of high beams when you are within 500 feet of another vehicle coming toward you or within 300 feet behind another vehicle.

questions.question: How should you change lanes?

options.text: Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal and check mirrors, then change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, turn on your signal. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no other vehicle is entering the same lane. Change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to turn left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: Turn from the lane closest to where you want to go. For a left turn on a one-way street, use the lane nearest to the left curb.

questions.question: You see flashing signals at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and look for a train.
Slow down and look for a train.
Look for a train, then speed up.
Do what the car ahead of you does.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and look for a train.
questions.explanation: Stop your car at least 15 feet from the tracks when you see flashing crossing signals or a lowered gate. Listen and look for an oncoming train before crossing.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning?

options.text: Keep your tires with good tread.
Reduce your speed when driving in rain.

questions.explanation: To prevent hydroplaning, keep your tires with good tread and properly inflated. Slow down when driving in rain. Hydroplaning happens most often at high speeds.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check for other vehicles in the lane.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and blind spot to make sure no vehicles are in your way. Always signal before you change lanes so other drivers know what you are doing.

questions.question: When driving near a large truck, you should:

options.text: Follow closely to reduce wind resistance on your car.
Avoid driving next to it for long periods.
Drive on its right side on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid driving next to it for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large trucks have large blind spots on both sides. Do not stay next to them for long periods of time.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in work zones?
questions.explanation: Orange signs, cones, and barriers mark work zones. Drive with extra caution when you see orange warning devices on the road.

questions.question: When it starts raining while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at the posted speed limit.
Drive close behind the car in front of you.

questions.explanation: Rain reduces how far you can see. Slow down and turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is very heavy and you cannot see clearly, pull to the side of the road and stop until the rain stops.

questions.question: When passing on a two-lane road, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn while you pass.
Flash your headlights while you pass.
Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check how far away oncoming vehicles are.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge how fast oncoming cars are traveling. They may be moving faster than they look. Make sure it is safe to change lanes before you pass. If you are not sure how fast an oncoming car is going, wait until it passes. Then pass only when you have enough space to change lanes safely.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your body?
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your body quickly but leaves slowly. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower your blood alcohol level. The only way to lower it is to wait.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look ahead farther than on a city street. Why?

options.text: Because it takes a quarter mile to stop your car.

questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes in traffic. Look for signals from other drivers. Cars will merge at on-ramps and interchanges. Be ready for sudden changes in road conditions and traffic flow.

questions.question: If another car is following you too closely on a two-lane road, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down gradually to let the tailgater pass you.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Tap your brakes, then go back to your normal speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually to let the tailgater pass you.
questions.explanation: If a car is following too closely, move to a different lane if you can. If you cannot change lanes, wait until the road is clear ahead and slow down gradually. This will encourage the other driver to pass you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign shows where pedestrians cross the road. Watch for people walking across the street.

questions.question: Two drivers reach a four-way stop sign at the same time. Who goes first?

options.text: One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.explanation: The driver on your right has the right-of-way at a four-way stop if you both arrive at the same time. You can then go when it is safe.

questions.question: You are parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Left, toward the center of the road.

questions.explanation: When parking downhill on any road, or uphill without a curb, turn your wheels toward the edge so your car rolls away from traffic if brakes fail. When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels toward the center so your car rolls into the curb if brakes fail.

questions.question: What happens when you drive while distracted?

options.text: You react more slowly to problems on the road.
It is only dangerous for young drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: You react more slowly to problems on the road.
questions.explanation: Distractions slow down how fast you can react to traffic and dangers. Distracted driving is never safe.

questions.question: What are "no zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear from view or are too close for the truck driver to stop or turn safely.
Areas behind the truck with enough space.
Areas with several car lengths of distance from the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear from view or are too close for the truck driver to stop or turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are places around trucks or buses where cars cannot be seen by the driver. They are also areas where a car is so close that it prevents the truck or bus driver from stopping or turning safely. A car in a "no zone" greatly increases the chance of a crash.

questions.question: After a police officer pulls you over, should you immediately get out of your vehicle and walk quickly toward the officer's car?
questions.explanation: Stay in your vehicle when stopped by police. Keep both hands visible on the steering wheel.

questions.question: You should not enter an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red. When is this rule true?

options.text: Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.explanation: Never enter an intersection unless you can drive completely across before the light turns red. Even if the light is green, blocking the intersection can result in a citation.

questions.question: What should you do to make sure your health does not cause unsafe driving?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Know how medicine affects your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.

questions.explanation: Your physical health affects your ability to drive safely. Know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at an intersection with multiple lanes. Oncoming traffic blocks your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up quickly when the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane as soon as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Only start a left turn when you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and safe.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What happens?

options.text: It may complete the turn in either of the two lanes.
It may have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
It must stay in the right lane the whole time.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need more space to turn. They often swing wide to complete a right turn.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire blows out while driving?

options.text: Apply the brake hard and hold it.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and use light braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and use light braking.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel tightly and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas pedal and braking lightly. Pull off the road safely when possible.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when may you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
After you wait for the light to change.
When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in the correct lane for a green arrow, you may proceed in that direction when the road ahead is clear. This applies whether the arrow appears alone or with another light.

questions.question: What is the correct order of traffic lights from top to bottom?
questions.explanation: Traffic lights are ordered from top to bottom as red, yellow, and green. Red is always at the top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, what must you do?

options.text: Stop and check for police cars.

questions.explanation: You may turn right on a green light unless a sign says otherwise. When turning, you must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: On a highway, there is a single broken white line next to you. What does this mean?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes going in the same direction. You may cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn in the direction the arrow points. In this case, you cannot turn right.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. What should you do?

options.text: Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and can hide in your blind spots. You must always look around carefully to spot them.

questions.question: When entering the freeway, you should drive at:

options.text: The same speed as the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same speed as the freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of traffic, unless traffic is above the legal speed limit.

questions.question: Why should you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane?
questions.explanation: A white cane means the person is blind. Slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
questions.explanation: Always wear both parts of a two-part seat belt. Using only one part does not protect you as well. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and go when the way is clear.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means "be careful." Slow down, look, and then proceed with care.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signals?

options.text: Only when pulling up to the curb.
When pulling up to or leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When pulling up to or leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Always signal when pulling up to a curb and when leaving a curb.

questions.question: What is the amount of alcohol in the blood called?
questions.explanation: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in your blood. A higher BAC means more impairment.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with a bicyclist ahead going the same direction. How should you pass?

options.text: Slow down, wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
Continue straight. It is the bicyclist's job to move out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to let the bicyclist know you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass with plenty of space between you and the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Pass a bicyclist like any other vehicle. Leave at least 3 feet of space on regular roads, or 5 feet on faster roads or with groups of bicyclists. Do not honk suddenly, as it may scare the rider and cause a crash.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Drive near all vehicles with caution.

questions.explanation: In snow and ice, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase your distance from other vehicles because slippery roads make it harder to stop.
